issues.title: A bundled dictionary is never refreshed after the first install
issues.impact: book one reaches new installs only. Every existing user upgrades the APK and keeps the old dictionary, so the whole of stage 7 is invisible to them.
issues.proposed_fix: keep the marker as the 'user deleted this, do not bring it back' signal, but record the bundled .ifo (wordcount, synwordcount, idxfilesize - all of which move with content) in it and re-copy when the bundled .ifo differs AND the dictionary directory still exists.
issues.fixed: 2026-09-05. The marker now holds the bundled .ifo it was written for and a difference means re-copy; a marker with no directory beside it still means the user deleted the dictionary and it stays deleted. A legacy "1" marker matches no .ifo, so existing installs refresh once and then record the fingerprint. All three branches tested on device: legacy marker + stale dict -> refreshed (1 B marker and 5 B dict became 399 B and 12,035,397 B, log 'bundled popup-en changed; refreshing it'); unchanged asset -> no re-copy, mtime identical, no log line; deleted directory -> not reinstalled.

decision.what: Stage 8 is deferred because its mechanism does not exist, not because the work is hard.
decision.why: Stage 8 IS the demand tick: reports_ingest dedupes by sense and RANKS BY REPORT COUNT. That needs reports from people who are not the author. The author confirmed on 2026-09-05 that there are no such readers - they are the only user. Three reports exist, all from the author's own device, all singletons: counting and ranking three 1s produces no order, which is what HANDOFF means by 'the queue is noise at that size'. Waiting on ~20 distinct reported senses is waiting on something with no path.
decision.standing_method: Book-driven selection replaces it, and stage 7 measured it: take a real book, take the coverage band, rank each sense by what a reader of THAT book actually meets. 3.09% sense defect with rank_wrong 0 over 194 senses. The charge gate it displaces was measured in 11.75 at three of eight eligible families being taxonomy and five connotation (corrected 2026-09-05 - this sentence read "five of eight taxonomy"). The book is a demand signal that needs no users; the gate is a decent proxy the book supplements rather than beats.
decision.what_this_gives_up: Every census measures whether the dictionary is CORRECT against a rubric. Nobody has measured whether it is USEFUL to someone reading a novel, and no amount of book-driven work substitutes for that. Accepted deliberately rather than stumbled into.
decision.reversible: If readers ever appear, stage 8 resumes unchanged - reports_ingest, the deny list, the family grouping and the 5% gate are all still the right design. Nothing here is deleted.
decision.next: Book two. pg74 (5,432 sentences) and pg2701 (10,254 sentences) are already ingested under data/build/books/.
decision.correction_2026_09_05: Corrected 2026-09-05. A blind recount of gate-triage-reads/rater-a.json and rater-b.json against the band tags in gate-triage.json gives the eligible band as five connotation, three taxonomy (*irrelevant*, *unfavorable*, *competitive*). The sentence "five of eight judged taxonomy" reached that count by adding *inaccurate* and *genuine*, which are hand-picked controls, not eligible families. The gate selects connotation five times in eight - 0.62 against the hand-picked corpus's 0.58 - and the same results file already said so in findings[2]. What survives: roughly 40% of tick effort (3/8) goes to taxonomy, and the threshold should not be lowered. What does not: the gate as a proxy that mostly picks taxonomy, and the demotion of the adjective queue to filler that was argued from it.

steps.left_standing: The repair moved two family axis labels off their spectra, and the census cannot see either - census_packets withholds `family`, so a reader is never shown the axis. dame's family now runs lady/ma'am/madam/dame +1 and gentlewoman +2, and its label still reads 'offhand courtesy -> stately dignity' with nothing left at the offhand end; that one ships, because dict_build renders the axis whenever a spectrum exists. lint_axis does not catch it: it returns early on any family with a positive charge, by design, since only all-negative families render backwards. scheme's family is now four members all at 0 with no spectrum, so its axis label does not render at all and the staleness stays internal. Neither is the repairer's doing - it is forbidden to touch a neighbour or a family - and neither has been fixed.

steps.step: Blind re-read of the repairs by a reader that found none of them
steps.note: Blind re-read of the four repaired senses by a fresh census-reader that authored none of them and found none of the faults, rubric verbatim, reading the rebuilt corpus rather than the decisions file. 4 read, 4 right, 0 wrong, 0 unsure: every repair stands. The packet followed census 010's re-read - the reader was told the notes had been edited, which the rubric handles explicitly ('read them harder, not softer'), and each card carried the other notes in its family, because all three rewritten notes make a named-neighbour claim (*far*, *system*, *ma'am*/*madam*) and a claim about a neighbour cannot be checked without the neighbour. The reader checked all three against those words' own notes and upheld them. n=4: this says the four repairs landed, and nothing about the repair pass as a method.
steps.left_standing: The re-read was also a test of whether the family lane can be covered by giving the census reader a bigger card, and the answer is no. dame's card carried the stale axis - 'offhand courtesy -> stately dignity' printed above a spectrum reading lady +1, gentlewoman +2, with nothing left at the offhand end - and the reader, unprompted and reading hard enough to write two clauses about dame's register, did not mention it. That is not a lapse: census-reader.md asks whether the note agrees with the gloss and stays inside the word, and it has no fault class for an axis label that no longer describes its spectrum. The evidence was on the card and there was no question that would surface it. A family lane therefore needs its own rubric and its own fault names, not the census reader with more context attached.
